title.en: Observed edges, inferred edges and disclosed coverage

summary: Require supporting records for asserted observed edges and disclose sampling and instrumentation coverage with the graph.
objective: Every observed edge resolves to supporting records, inferred edges are labelled, and coverage and window are stated.
applies_when: A graph is derived from observations rather than authored by hand.
The observation pipeline samples or misses some events.
A reader might treat the graph as a complete map.
intent_signals: how much of the system is instrumented here
example_prompts: Audit the evidence behind the edges in this service graph.

principles: An asserted observed edge needs supporting records; an edge drawn because it seems likely is a hypothesis and must be labelled as one.

Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence, because sampling and instrumentation gaps mean a missing connection may exist and simply not be recorded. The converse also holds: an edge seen in only one window is still observed evidence, and what is unestablished is its persistence, not the observation.
Coverage is part of the result, so the artifact should state what is instrumented and what sampling was in effect.
implementation: For every displayed edge record the supporting input records or the fact that it is inferred, keeping the two categories distinct in the data and in the display.
Record the sampling configuration and the observation window with the dataset and show them with the graph.
List components known to exist but absent from the data, so absence is explicit rather than implied by a blank area.

Re-run the extraction over a second window and report per-window presence and observation counts for every edge, so an edge seen in one window keeps its evidence while its persistence stays unestablished.
observable_checks: Every asserted observed edge resolves to supporting records, and inferred edges stay labelled everywhere they appear, including in exports.
The artifact states the sampling configuration and observation window, so a reader cannot mistake a sampled view for a complete map.

Edges present in only one window are reported with their window and count and their persistence marked unestablished, rather than being downgraded as unreliable; a union across windows is legitimate when it is labelled as a union with its combined window.

known_limits: An evidence and disclosure procedure; it does not improve instrumentation coverage or validate the correctness of the underlying telemetry.
Authored verification guidance; no dataset was extracted for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: Sampling reduces the traces that are collected and exported: head sampling decides as early as possible without seeing the whole trace, tail sampling decides after considering most spans of a trace, and traces that are not sampled are not processed or exported.
claims.scope: The sampling behaviour described in the cited documentation; the consequences for a specific dataset depend on its own configuration.
